mcqs.question: What is ice?
mcqs.explanation: Ice is the solid state of water; it has a fixed shape and volume, unlike liquid water which flows. Option B correctly identifies ice as solid water, while the other options describe different states or substances.

mcqs.question: Which statement best describes liquid water?

options.A: It has a fixed shape and volume
options.B: It takes the shape of its container but has a fixed volume
options.C: It expands to fill any space

mcqs.answer: It takes the shape of its container but has a fixed volume
mcqs.explanation: Liquid water flows, so it adopts the shape of the container it is in, yet its volume remains constant. Option B captures this property; the other options describe solids, gases, or are incorrect.

mcqs.question: Water vapour differs from steam in that:

options.A: Water vapour is an invisible gas, while steam consists of visible tiny droplets
options.B: Water vapour is a solid, steam is a liquid
options.C: Water vapour is colder than steam
options.D: Water vapour is the same as ice

mcqs.answer: Water vapour is an invisible gas, while steam consists of visible tiny droplets
mcqs.explanation: Water vapour is the gaseous phase of water and cannot be seen. When water condenses into tiny droplets it becomes visible steam. Option A states this distinction; the other options are scientifically incorrect.

mcqs.learning_point: Observable properties of the three states
mcqs.question: Which set correctly matches each state of water with one of its observable properties?

options.A: Ice – takes the shape of its container; water – invisible; steam – has a rigid shape
options.B: Ice – rigid shape; water – takes the shape of its container; steam – invisible gas
options.C: Ice – invisible gas; water – rigid shape; steam – takes the shape of its container
options.D: Ice – expands when heated; water – contracts when heated; steam – is a solid

mcqs.answer: Ice – rigid shape; water – takes the shape of its container; steam – invisible gas
mcqs.explanation: Ice (solid) keeps a fixed shape, liquid water flows to fill the shape of its container, and steam (water vapour) is an invisible gas. Option B lists these correctly; the other options mix up properties or are false.

mcqs.learning_point: Water changing from one state to another
mcqs.question: When water is heated on a stove and turns into steam, which process is occurring?
mcqs.explanation: Heating liquid water causes it to change into water vapour, a process called evaporation. Condensation is the reverse, sublimation is solid to gas, and freezing is liquid to solid. Hence, option C is correct.

mcqs.question: A child places a bottle of water in a freezer. After several hours the water becomes solid. Which term best describes this change?
mcqs.explanation: When liquid water loses heat and becomes solid ice, the process is called freezing. Melting is solid to liquid, boiling is liquid to gas, and condensation is gas to liquid. Therefore, option B correctly names the process.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about liquid water is a common misconception?

options.A: It always has the same shape regardless of the container
options.B: It takes the shape of the container it is placed in
options.C: It is invisible to the naked eye
options.D: It can flow and be poured

mcqs.answer: It always has the same shape regardless of the container
mcqs.explanation: The misconception is that liquid water has a fixed shape. In reality, liquid water conforms to the shape of its container (option B). Options C and D are true statements about liquid water, while option A is the false belief being tested.

mcqs.question: When a pot of boiling water is covered with a lid, the lid becomes wet. Why does this happen?

options.A: Water vapour condenses on the cooler lid, forming droplets
options.B: Steam freezes on the lid turning into ice
options.C: Liquid water evaporates from the lid itself
options.D: Heat directly turns the lid into water

mcqs.answer: Water vapour condenses on the cooler lid, forming droplets
mcqs.explanation: The hot water produces water vapour (steam). When this vapour contacts the cooler lid, it loses energy and changes back to liquid water, forming droplets—condensation. The other options describe processes that do not occur under these conditions.
